ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Dark Star → Eleven sequence with soaring Lovelight
ai_show_review.blurb: The set opens with a blazing Dark Star that segues into Saint Stephen and rockets through The Eleven at mach speed. Pigpen’s Turn On Your Lovelight closes the set with soulful vocal power. Soundboard recordings capture the performance despite modest fidelity.
ai_show_review.review: August 28, 1968 at the Avalon Ballroom finds the Dead in top form, delivering a single‑set blaze that still feels fresh today. The night kicks off with an incandescent Dark Star that builds into Saint Stephen before launching into a high‑octane Eleven—Jerry’s lead slicing through the mix like a jet engine while Phil locks in tight bass support. After a brief dip on Death Don't Have No Mercy, Pigpen lifts the vibe with a soulful Turn On Your Lovelight, his harmonica and vocals adding that classic Avalon grit. While the available soundboard tapes suffer from low volume and some muddy EQ, they still convey the raw excitement of the performance; the Vernon source is the clearest window into this historic set.

best_recording.reason: Fair‑quality soundboard capture with clearer volume and less processing, preserving the full first set.

key_highlights: Blazing Dark Star that segues seamlessly into Saint Stephen
Soulful Turn On Your Lovelight featuring Pigpen’s vocal power
Overall high‑energy performance despite modest soundboard fidelity

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers a beautiful Dark Star solo and flies through The Eleven at "mach speed", adding strong leads on Lovelight.
band_performance.Phil: Stays close behind Jerry during the Eleven, providing solid bass support throughout the set.
